summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted after accidental dislodgement of his tunneled Remodulin catheter while showering. He developed febrile neutropenia on hospital day 2 with a white blood cell count of 0.7 and ANC of 234, likely due to recent gastroenteritis from consuming rancid butter. He was treated with vancomycin and Zosyn for 3 days, remained afebrile after day 3, and blood cultures were negative. A new tunneled central line was placed on hospital day 4 after platelet transfusion and confirmation of no active infection. His portopulmonary hypertension remained stable on Remodulin 45 ng/kg/min and sildenafil, with no change in oxygen requirements. Hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia were managed with supplementation, and magnesium oxide was increased to 800 mg daily. He was discharged home with outpatient follow-up in hematology, pulmonology, and hepatology, and instructions to monitor weight and catheter site.
